#!/bin/bash
#
# Multi-Turn PPO on Endless Terminals with Qwen3-1.7B, on slime v0.3.2.
#
# The run has two stages:
#
#   Stage A -- "the previous training run".  A real PPO rollout (actor + critic)
#              starting from the base HF model, which saves a Megatron
#              checkpoint for both roles.
#
#   Stage B -- "the model was reloaded".  The actor genuinely resumes from
#              Stage A's Megatron checkpoint (weights *and* optimizer state).
#              The critic's backbone is reloaded from the base model.  Stage B
#              opens with NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts (the
#              warmup window) and then trains actor and critic jointly.
#
# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (slime/) and is the
# copy that runs -- this script puts it ahead of the image's install on
# PYTHONPATH, so editing slime/ here is what takes effect, with nothing to
# install first.
#
# NOTE ON A SHARED HOST: unlike slime's own example scripts this one never runs
# `pkill -9 ray / pkill -9 python / ray stop --force` on entry.  It is meant to
# run inside its own container, and it brings up a private Ray head on a
# non-default port with a private temp dir.

set -euo pipefail

WS="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"

# The container runs as root while /workspace is a bind mount owned by whoever
# checked the case out, so any .pyc written here lands root-owned in their tree
# -- and `importlib` copies the *source* file's mode onto the .pyc, so a 600
# source yields a 600 root-owned file that even the owner cannot read, and
# `cp -r` of the case fails. Nothing here benefits from a bytecode cache.
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1

MODEL_DIR="${MODEL_DIR:-${WS}/Qwen3-1.7B}"
ET_SRC="${ET_SRC:-${WS}/endless-terminals}"
SLIME_HOME="${SLIME_HOME:-${WS}/slime}"
OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR:-${WS}/outputs}"
CKPT_ROOT="${CKPT_ROOT:-/ckpt}"

# Endless Terminals sandbox knobs; also forwarded into the Ray workers, which
# read them at import time in et/rollout.py.
#
# These must NOT live under /dev/shm: it is mounted noexec in the training
# image, and many tasks' verifiers assert os.access(path, os.X_OK), which is
# False there even at mode 755.
export ET_DATA_ROOT="${ET_DATA_ROOT:-/tmp/et_prompts}"
export ET_SCRATCH="${ET_SCRATCH:-/tmp/et_episodes}"
export ET_MAX_TURNS="${ET_MAX_TURNS:-6}"
export ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS="${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS:-384}"
export ET_CMD_TIMEOUT="${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT:-20}"
export ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS="${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS:-1200}"

NUM_GPUS="${NUM_GPUS:-2}"
TP_SIZE="${TP_SIZE:-2}"
SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION="${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION:-0.55}"
# Rollouts per stage. Both stages use the same count on purpose, and must:
# slime derives `train_iters` from `--num-rollout` (model.py:203) and Megatron
# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons inside the checkpoint, then
# asserts on reload that they match the ones the new arguments imply
# ("total number of iterations do not match"). Giving Stage B a different
# rollout count than Stage A would trip that assert before any training runs.
# In Stage A these rollouts are ordinary PPO; Stage B opens with
# NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts -- the warmup window -- and then
# trains actor and critic jointly for the rest.
NUM_ROLLOUTS="${NUM_ROLLOUTS:-2}"
# Stage B is the long one: critic warmup followed by joint PPO, trained until
# the validation pass rate stops moving. It no longer has to match Stage A's
# rollout count -- see --override-opt-param-scheduler at the submit site.
NUM_ROLLOUTS_B="${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS}}"
# Rollouts at the start of Stage B in which only the critic trains. This is the
# warmup window the incident was reported against, and the window in which the
# value loss is measured.
NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS="${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}}"

# Episodes per rollout = ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE x N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT; optimizer
# steps per rollout = that, divided by GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE.
ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE="${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT="${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-2}"
GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE="${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
LR="${LR:-1e-6}"

# How many leading critic optimizer steps the reported warmup statistics cover.
# Derived rather than guessed, because once Stage B runs past the critic-only
# phase the two are no longer the same thing: averaging the value loss over all
# of a 30-rollout Stage B measures mostly a critic that has already been
# trained, which is not what "warmup value loss" names and not what the
# incident was about.
CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=$(( NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS * ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT / GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE ))
[ "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" -gt 0 ] || CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=1

# Held-out evaluation during Stage B. 0 disables it, which is what the short
# value-loss-only reproduction wants.
#
# val and test get different sample budgets. val only has to say *when* the
# curve flattens, so 2 samples x 150 tasks is enough; test carries the
# end-to-end claim and is compared per task, where the useful quantity is each
# task's success *rate*, which 1 or 2 samples cannot resolve at all.
EVAL_INTERVAL="${EVAL_INTERVAL:-0}"
N_EVAL_SAMPLES="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES:-2}"
N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST:-4}"

# How often Stage B checkpoints. Trained to convergence, Stage B runs for well
# over an hour, which on a shared host is long enough to be interrupted -- two
# runs of this case were killed from outside the container mid-training, once
# with SIGTERM and once with SIGKILL. So Stage B saves as it goes and a second
# invocation picks up where the first stopped, instead of starting the hour
# again. 0 disables it, which is what the short value-loss-only reproduction
# wants: it writes nothing and measures only the reload.
STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL="${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL:-0}"

RAY_PORT="${RAY_PORT:-6479}"
DASH_PORT="${DASH_PORT:-8277}"
RAY_TMP="${RAY_TMP:-/tmp/ray_ppo}"

mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}" "${CKPT_ROOT}" "${ET_SCRATCH}"

# --------------------------------------------------------- 0. the slime source
# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (${SLIME_HOME}) and is
# put ahead of the image's editable install on PYTHONPATH below, so it is the
# copy that trains -- there is nothing to install first.
test -f "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" || {
    echo "FATAL: bundled slime source not found at ${SLIME_HOME}" >&2
    exit 1
}

# ------------------------------------------------------- 1. the prompt dataset
# prepare.sh ships the already-built dataset (transpiled + validated + split) at
# ${WS}/et_prompts. Seed ET_DATA_ROOT from it so the build below is skipped: the
# 2492->1489 admission is environment-fixed and reproducible, so there is no need
# to re-run the ~40min transpile+validate pass (and ET_SRC is never read). The
# copy lands in a writable, exec-capable dir (ET_DATA_ROOT defaults to /tmp) --
# the bundled tree under /workspace may be a root-owned bind mount. If the
# prebuilt payload is absent, fall through to building from ET_SRC as before.
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ] && [ -s "${WS}/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
    echo "=== seeding ET_DATA_ROOT from prebuilt ${WS}/et_prompts (skipping transpile+validate) ==="
    mkdir -p "${ET_DATA_ROOT}"
    cp -a "${WS}/et_prompts/." "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/"
fi
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
    echo "=== transpiling + validating the Endless Terminals tasks ==="
    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.build_dataset --src "${ET_SRC}" --out "${ET_DATA_ROOT}") \
        2>&1 | tee "${OUT_DIR}/build_dataset.log"
fi
# Deliberately not silenced. A report that is quietly 0 bytes is worse than one
# that is loudly absent: it reads as "every task was rejected" to anyone who
# opens it later, and that has happened here more than once.
copy_artifact() {   # copy_artifact <src>
    local src="$1" dst="${OUT_DIR}/$(basename "$1")"
    if ! cp -f "${src}" "${dst}"; then
        echo "WARNING: could not copy ${src} into ${OUT_DIR}" >&2
    elif [ ! -s "${dst}" ] && [ -s "${src}" ]; then
        echo "WARNING: ${dst} came out empty although ${src} is not" >&2
    fi
}
copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/validation_report.json"
N_PROMPTS="$(wc -l < "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")"
echo "prompt set: ${N_PROMPTS} validated Endless Terminals tasks"
if [ "${N_PROMPTS}" -lt 4 ]; then
    echo "FATAL: too few tasks survived validation to train on." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Train on one part of the task set and measure on another. The split is a pure
# function of the admitted list and a fixed seed, so every run trains and is
# scored on exactly the same tasks -- otherwise a comparison between runs is
# partly measuring which tasks each one happened to get.
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl" ]; then
    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")
fi
copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/splits.json"
TRAIN_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl"
VAL_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_val.jsonl"
TEST_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_test.jsonl"
printf 'splits: train %s / val %s / test %s\n' \
    "$(wc -l < "${TRAIN_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${VAL_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${TEST_SPLIT}")"

# ------------------------------------------------------------- 2. shared args
source "${WS}/configs/model_args.sh"

ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
    --prompt-data "${TRAIN_SPLIT}"
    --input-key prompt
    --label-key label
    --rollout-shuffle
    --rollout-batch-size "${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE}"
    --n-samples-per-prompt "${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT}"
    --rollout-max-response-len 2048
    --rollout-temperature 1.0
    --global-batch-size "${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE}"
    --balance-data
    # The multi-turn terminal loop and its pytest-based episode reward.
    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate
    --custom-rm-path et.rollout.reward_func
)

PPO_ARGS=(
    --advantage-estimator ppo   # -> args.use_critic
    --gamma 1.0
    --lambd 1.0
    --eps-clip 0.2
    --value-clip 0.2
    --kl-coef 0.0               # no reference model, hence no --ref-load and
    --entropy-coef 0.0          # no HF -> torch_dist conversion step
)

PERF_ARGS=(
    --tensor-model-parallel-size "${TP_SIZE}"
    --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
    --context-parallel-size 1
    --recompute-granularity full
    --recompute-method uniform
    --recompute-num-layers 1
    --use-dynamic-batch-size
    --max-tokens-per-gpu 8192
)
# Sequence parallelism splits the activations of the non-tensor-parallel ops
# across the TP group, so it is only defined for TP > 1; Megatron asserts on it.
# Spelled as an `if` rather than `[ ... ] && ...`: the latter evaluates to the
# test's status, which under `set -e` ends the script whenever TP_SIZE is 1.
if [ "${TP_SIZE}" -gt 1 ]; then
    PERF_ARGS+=(--sequence-parallel)
fi

OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
    --optimizer adam
    --lr "${LR}"
    --lr-decay-style constant
    --weight-decay 0.0
    --adam-beta1 0.9
    --adam-beta2 0.95
)

SGLANG_ARGS=(
    --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine "${NUM_GPUS}"
    # Colocated: this fraction is what SGLang keeps, and Megatron's weights,
    # gradients and Adam state have to fit in the rest. At TP 2 each GPU carries
    # half of each role, so 0.55 leaves enough; drop it when NUM_GPUS is 1 and
    # one device has to hold both roles whole.
    --sglang-mem-fraction-static "${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION}"
)

# Held-out scoring, used only by Stage B. slime evaluates once before the first
# rollout and then every EVAL_INTERVAL rollouts, which gives both the starting
# pass rate and the curve that says whether training has converged.
#
# val and test are evaluated at the same points on purpose. The convergence
# *decision* is read off val; test is reported only at the final point, and
# evaluating it throughout costs generation but no statistical validity, since
# nothing about the run is conditioned on it.
#
# Spelled as an --eval-config YAML rather than --eval-prompt-data because the
# two splits need different sample counts, and --n-samples-per-eval-prompt is
# one global number. Everything the YAML leaves out still falls back to the
# command line (eval_config.py:10 DATASET_RUNTIME_SPECS), so temperature,
# response length and the prompt/label keys are set once, below and above.
EVAL_ARGS=()
if [ "${EVAL_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ]; then
    cat > "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml" <<YAML
eval:
  datasets:
    - name: et_val
      path: ${VAL_SPLIT}
      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES}
    - name: et_test
      path: ${TEST_SPLIT}
      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST}
YAML
    EVAL_ARGS=(
        --eval-interval "${EVAL_INTERVAL}"
        --eval-config "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml"
        --eval-max-response-len 2048
        --eval-temperature 1.0
        --log-passrate
        --custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data
    )
fi

MISC_ARGS=(
    --attention-dropout 0.0
    --hidden-dropout 0.0
    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
    --attention-softmax-in-fp32
    --attention-backend flash
    --seed 1234
)

# --------------------------------------------------------- 3. per-role configs
# Actor and critic share `args.save` by default, which would make them clobber
# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the
# actor's is [vocab, hidden_size]), so each role gets its own directory.
cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" <<YAML
# Stage A: "the previous training run". Both roles start from the base model.
megatron:
  - name: stage-a-actor
    role: actor
    overrides:
      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor
  - name: stage-a-critic
    role: critic
    overrides:
      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic
YAML

# Stage B can be entered two ways, and they are not the same event.
#
#   fresh   -- "the model was reloaded". The actor resumes from Stage A's
#              Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base
#              model.
#
#   resume  -- an interrupted Stage B being continued. Both roles load Stage B's
#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included, and the run continues
#              from the last saved rollout. The first attempt's log is kept,
#              not overwritten (see the STAGE_B_LOG choice below).
STAGE_B_RESUME=0
if [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ] \
   && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
    STAGE_B_RESUME=1
fi

if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic"
else
    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/actor"
    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${MODEL_DIR}"
fi

cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml" <<YAML
# Stage B, $([ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ] && echo "resumed from its own checkpoints" || echo "entered fresh after a reload").
megatron:
  - name: stage-b-actor
    role: actor
    overrides:
      load: ${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor
  - name: stage-b-critic
    role: critic
    overrides:
      load: ${STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic
YAML

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- 4. ray
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

ray start --head \
    --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 \
    --port "${RAY_PORT}" \
    --num-gpus "${NUM_GPUS}" \
    --disable-usage-stats \
    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 \
    --dashboard-port "${DASH_PORT}" \
    --temp-dir "${RAY_TMP}"
trap 'ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT

# `|| true` on the whole pipeline, not decoration: under `pipefail` a `grep`
# that matches nothing fails the pipeline, so on a host with no NVLink -- or in
# a container holding a single GPU, where the topology matrix has no peer links
# to report -- `set -e` would kill the script here. Silently: this sits between
# `ray start` and the first echo of Stage A, so the log just stops.
NVLINK_COUNT="$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l || true)"
HAS_NVLINK=0
[ "${NVLINK_COUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] && HAS_NVLINK=1

RUNTIME_ENV_JSON="{
  \"env_vars\": {
    \"PYTHONPATH\": \"/root/Megatron-LM/:${SLIME_HOME}:${WS}\",
    \"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\": \"1\",
    \"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\": \"${HAS_NVLINK}\",
    \"ET_DATA_ROOT\": \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\",
    \"ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR\": \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_episodes\",
    \"ET_SCRATCH\": \"${ET_SCRATCH}\",
    \"ET_MAX_TURNS\": \"${ET_MAX_TURNS}\",
    \"ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS\": \"${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS}\",
    \"ET_CMD_TIMEOUT\": \"${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT}\",
    \"ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS\": \"${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS}\"
  }
}"

submit() {   # submit <log-file> <extra args...>
    local log="$1"; shift
    # The entrypoint is an absolute path on purpose: `ray job submit` does not
    # run it in this shell's directory but in the cwd of the Ray head (here
    # /workspace, since no `working_dir` is uploaded), so a bare `train.py`
    # would not be found. Running ${SLIME_HOME}/train.py puts the bundled slime
    # tree on the driver's sys.path[0]; the ray workers get it from ${SLIME_HOME}
    # on PYTHONPATH (RUNTIME_ENV_JSON above), ahead of the image's install.
    ray job submit \
        --address "http://127.0.0.1:${DASH_PORT}" \
        --runtime-env-json "${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
        -- python3 "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" \
        --actor-num-nodes 1 \
        --actor-num-gpus-per-node "${NUM_GPUS}" \
        --colocate \
        --hf-checkpoint "${MODEL_DIR}" \
        "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${PPO_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${PERF_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${SGLANG_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${MISC_ARGS[@]}" \
        "$@" 2>&1 | tee "${log}"
}

# Ray forwards actor stdout to the job driver, but keep the raw worker logs too:
# the per-step metrics are emitted by the train actors, not by the driver.
collect_worker_logs() {   # collect_worker_logs <tag>
    # Two statements, not one: `local a=.. b=..` expands every word before it
    # assigns any of them, so referring to ${tag} on the same line would read
    # it while it is still unset -- fatal under `set -u`.
    local tag="$1"
    local dst="${OUT_DIR}/${tag}_worker_logs"
    mkdir -p "${dst}"
    grep -rl "critic-step" "${RAY_TMP}"/session_*/logs/ 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
        cp -f "${f}" "${dst}/$(basename "$(dirname "${f}")")_$(basename "${f}")" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. stage A
echo
echo "############ Stage A: the previous training run ############"
# SKIP_STAGE_A=1 reuses a checkpoint an earlier invocation already wrote, for
# re-running the long Stage B after an interruption. Off by default, and
# refuses to be silently wrong: with no checkpoint there, Stage A runs anyway.
if [ "${SKIP_STAGE_A:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
    echo "SKIP_STAGE_A=1 and ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor already holds a checkpoint -- reusing it."
else
    submit "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
        --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" \
        --load "${MODEL_DIR}" \
        --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" \
        --save-interval 1 \
        --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS}" \
        --num-critic-only-steps 0
    collect_worker_logs stage_a
fi

echo
echo "checkpoint written by Stage A:"
ls -1 "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" 2>/dev/null || true
test -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" || {
    echo "FATAL: Stage A did not produce a resumable Megatron checkpoint." >&2
    exit 1

475	    --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}"
476	    --num-critic-only-steps "${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS}"
477	)
478	
479	STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log"
480	if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
481	    # The first attempt's log holds the warmup window that the value-loss
482	    # verdict is read from, so a resume must not overwrite it.
483	    n=1
484	    while [ -e "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
485	    STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log"
486	    echo "resuming Stage B from ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_{actor,critic}" \
487	         "(iteration $(cat "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt")); log -> ${STAGE_B_LOG}"
488	    # --start-rollout-id is deliberately NOT passed here. slime takes the start
489	    # id from the *critic*'s loaded checkpoint when a critic is in play
490	    # (placement_group.py:212), and Stage B saves at `iteration = rollout_id`,
491	    # so omitting it resumes at exactly the rollout after the last saved one.
492	else
493	    # --start-rollout-id 0 pins the warmup window: without it the start id is
494	    # inferred from whichever checkpoint the critic loaded, and on a fresh
495	    # Stage B the critic loads a plain HF directory (iteration 0).
496	    STAGE_B_ARGS+=(--start-rollout-id 0)
497	fi
498	
499	submit "${STAGE_B_LOG}" "${STAGE_B_ARGS[@]}" "${EVAL_ARGS[@]+"${EVAL_ARGS[@]}"}"
500	collect_worker_logs stage_b
501	
502	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. verdict
503	echo
504	echo "############ critic warmup value loss ############"
505	python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
506	    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log" \
507	    --warmup-steps "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" \
508	    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_value_loss.json"
509	
510	python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
511	    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
512	    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a_value_loss.json" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
513	
514	echo
515	echo "artifacts in ${OUT_DIR}:"
516	ls -1 "${OUT_DIR}"
517

if [ -n "${AUTORLBENCH_STAGE:-}" ]; then
    if [ -r /etc/autorlbench-image-path ]; then
        _autorlbench_image_path=""
        IFS= read -r _autorlbench_image_path < /etc/autorlbench-image-path || :
        _autorlbench_missing=""
        _autorlbench_ifs=$IFS
        IFS=:
        for _autorlbench_dir in $_autorlbench_image_path; do
            [ -n "$_autorlbench_dir" ] || continue
            case ":$_autorlbench_missing:$PATH:" in
                *":$_autorlbench_dir:"*) ;;
                *) _autorlbench_missing="${_autorlbench_missing:+$_autorlbench_missing:}$_autorlbench_dir" ;;
            esac

# Adapt from https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b1efb3c7126ef7615e8c333432d76e08038e17ff/pretrain_gpt.py
import argparse
import inspect
import re
from contextlib import nullcontext
from typing import Literal

import torch
from megatron.core import tensor_parallel
from megatron.core.models.gpt import GPTModel
from megatron.core.models.gpt.gpt_layer_specs import (
    get_gpt_decoder_block_spec,
    get_gpt_layer_local_spec,
    get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_spec,
)
from megatron.core.transformer.spec_utils import import_module
from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config import TransformerConfig
from megatron.training.arguments import core_transformer_config_from_args

from slime.utils.misc import load_function

_INDEXER_DIRECT_SUBMODULE_NAMES = frozenset(
    {
        "wq_b",
        "wk",
        "k_norm",
        "weights_proj",
        "index_kpool_compress_ape",
        "index_kpool_compress_gate",
    }
)


def _is_indexer_parameter(name: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether *name* belongs to a DSA indexer.

    The GLM plugin exposes indexer projections directly under
    ``self_attention``. Megatron's upstream DSA implementation instead nests
    them under ``self_attention.core_attention.indexer``. Keep the ownership
    check structural so similarly named non-indexer projections stay trainable.
    """

    parts = name.split(".")
    for index, part in enumerate(parts):
        if part != "self_attention" or index + 1 >= len(parts):
            continue
        attention_parts = parts[index + 1 :]
        if attention_parts[0] in _INDEXER_DIRECT_SUBMODULE_NAMES:
            return True
        if "indexer" in attention_parts[:-1]:
            return True
    return False


# Adapt from https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/c3b20575d2bc815fcccd84bddb4c0401fc4b632b/verl/models/llama/megatron/layers/parallel_linear.py#L82
class LinearForLastLayer(torch.nn.Linear):
    # WORKSPACE CHANGE, part of the shared setup: `bias` defaults to False
    # here, where upstream slime v0.3.2 defaults it to True.
    #
    # Upstream cannot load a critic from a HuggingFace checkpoint at all. The
    # HF loader walks every Megatron parameter and asks the model's mapper for
    # a source tensor; `output_layer.weight` is special-cased (a [1, hidden]
    # value head is skipped when the HF tensor is [vocab, hidden]), but
    # `output_layer.bias` has no HF counterpart and no special case, so
    # `qwen_hf_tensor` raises KeyError("Unsupported Megatron parameter
    # 'output_layer.bias'") before training starts. See
    # slime/backends/megatron_utils/hf_to_megatron/{qwen,common}.py.
    #
    # A value head does not need a bias -- it is one scalar of freedom that
    # V(s) can equally express through the backbone -- and dropping it is the
    # smallest change that lets a critic start from HF weights, which is what
    # Stage B does.
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_size: int,
        output_size: int,
        *,
        config: TransformerConfig,
        bias: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(in_features=input_size, out_features=output_size, bias=bias)
        self.sequence_parallel = config.sequence_parallel
        if self.sequence_parallel:
            self.weight.sequence_parallel = True
            if bias:
                self.bias.sequence_parallel = True

        init_method_std = getattr(config, "init_method_std", None)
        if init_method_std is None:
            init_method_std = 0.02
        self.weight.data.normal_(mean=0.0, std=init_method_std)
        if bias:
            self.bias.data.zero_()

    def forward(
        self,
        input_: torch.Tensor,
        weight: torch.Tensor | None = None,
        runtime_gather_output: bool | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, None]:
        logits = super().forward(input_)
        logits = logits.float()
        if self.sequence_parallel:
            logits = tensor_parallel.gather_from_sequence_parallel_region(logits, tensor_parallel_output_grad=False)
        return logits, None


def _get_model_provider_func(
    args: argparse.Namespace,
    role: Literal["actor", "critic"] = "actor",
):
    # Support custom model provider path (similar to --custom-rm-path for reward models)
    if getattr(args, "custom_model_provider_path", None):

        def wrapped_model_provider(
            pre_process: bool = True, post_process: bool = True, vp_stage: int | None = None
        ) -> GPTModel:
            custom_model_provider = load_function(args.custom_model_provider_path)
            # Check if the custom provider supports vp_stage parameter
            has_vp_stage = "vp_stage" in inspect.signature(custom_model_provider).parameters

56	class LinearForLastLayer(torch.nn.Linear):
57	    # WORKSPACE CHANGE, part of the shared setup: `bias` defaults to False
58	    # here, where upstream slime v0.3.2 defaults it to True.
59	    #
60	    # Upstream cannot load a critic from a HuggingFace checkpoint at all. The
61	    # HF loader walks every Megatron parameter and asks the model's mapper for
62	    # a source tensor; `output_layer.weight` is special-cased (a [1, hidden]
63	    # value head is skipped when the HF tensor is [vocab, hidden]), but
64	    # `output_layer.bias` has no HF counterpart and no special case, so
65	    # `qwen_hf_tensor` raises KeyError("Unsupported Megatron parameter
66	    # 'output_layer.bias'") before training starts. See
67	    # slime/backends/megatron_utils/hf_to_megatron/{qwen,common}.py.
68	    #
69	    # A value head does not need a bias -- it is one scalar of freedom that
70	    # V(s) can equally express through the backbone -- and dropping it is the
71	    # smallest change that lets a critic start from HF weights, which is what
72	    # Stage B does.
73	    def __init__(
74	        self,
75	        input_size: int,
76	        output_size: int,
77	        *,
78	        config: TransformerConfig,
79	        bias: bool = False,
80	    ) -> None:
81	        super().__init__(in_features=input_size, out_features=output_size, bias=bias)
82	        self.sequence_parallel = config.sequence_parallel
83	        if self.sequence_parallel:
84	            self.weight.sequence_parallel = True
85	            if bias:
86	                self.bias.sequence_parallel = True
87	
88	        init_method_std = getattr(config, "init_method_std", None)
89	        if init_method_std is None:
90	            init_method_std = 0.02
91	        self.weight.data.normal_(mean=0.0, std=init_method_std)
92	        if bias:
93	            self.bias.data.zero_()
94	
95	    def forward(
96	        self,
97	        input_: torch.Tensor,
98	        weight: torch.Tensor | None = None,
99	        runtime_gather_output: bool | None = None,
100	    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, None]:
101	        logits = super().forward(input_)
102	        logits = logits.float()
103	        if self.sequence_parallel:
104	            logits = tensor_parallel.gather_from_sequence_parallel_region(logits, tensor_parallel_output_grad=False)
105	        return logits, None

return get_checkpoint_name(load_dir, iteration, release, return_base_dir=True)


def _critic_output_layer_needs_reinit(args: Namespace, model: Sequence[DDP], role: str) -> bool:
    if role != "critic" or args.load is None:
        return False

    from megatron.core.dist_checkpointing.serialization import load_tensors_metadata

    checkpoint_path = Path(get_load_checkpoint_path_by_args(args))
    if not (checkpoint_path / ".metadata").is_file():
        return False

    checkpoint_metadata = load_tensors_metadata(str(checkpoint_path))
    for _chunk_id, output_layer in _iter_critic_output_layers(model):
        for name in ("weight", "bias"):
            param = getattr(output_layer, name, None)
            if param is None:
                continue

            param_name = f"output_layer.{name}"
            ckpt_tensor_metadata = next(
                (
                    tensor_metadata
                    for key, tensor_metadata in checkpoint_metadata.items()
                    if key == param_name or key.endswith(f".{param_name}")
                ),
                None,
            )
            expected_shape = tuple(param.shape)
            checkpoint_shape = tuple(ckpt_tensor_metadata.global_shape) if ckpt_tensor_metadata is not None else None
            if checkpoint_shape == expected_shape:
                continue

            reason = (
                "missing from checkpoint metadata"
                if checkpoint_shape is None
                else f"shape mismatch checkpoint={checkpoint_shape} runtime={expected_shape}"
            )
            logger.warning(
                "Will reinitialize critic %s after checkpoint load because it is %s",
                param_name,
                reason,
            )
            return True

    return False


@torch.no_grad()
def _reinitialize_critic_output_layer(args: Namespace, model: Sequence[DDP]) -> None:
    init_method_std = getattr(args, "init_method_std", None)
    if init_method_std is None:
        init_method_std = 0.02
    for _chunk_id, output_layer in _iter_critic_output_layers(model):
        output_layer.weight.data.normal_(mean=0.0, std=init_method_std)
        if output_layer.bias is not None:
            output_layer.bias.data.zero_()


def get_optimizer_param_scheduler(args: Namespace, optimizer: MegatronOptimizer) -> OptimizerParamScheduler:
    """Create and configure the optimizer learning-rate/weight-decay scheduler.

    This configures iteration-based schedules derived from the global batch size
    and run-time arguments.

    Args:
        args (Namespace): Training/runtime arguments (argparse namespace).
        optimizer (MegatronOptimizer): Megatron optimizer bound to the model.

    Returns:
        OptimizerParamScheduler: Initialized scheduler bound to ``optimizer``.
    """
    # Iteration-based training. ``train_iters`` is an estimate of the total
    # number of training steps — it's only used to size Megatron's LR decay
    # schedule (and ``lr_decay_iters`` defaults to it). With variable per-rollout
    # sample counts (dynamic sampling / filtering / custom step splitter) the
    # *actual* total can drift; the schedule still tracks the true progress via
    # ``opt_param_scheduler.num_steps`` (samples consumed, also persisted across
    # resume), so the worst case is the cosine/linear schedule reaches its
    # plateau slightly early or late. Pass ``--lr-decay-iters`` explicitly if you
    # need exact decay control.
    args.train_iters = args.num_rollout * args.rollout_batch_size * args.n_samples_per_prompt // args.global_batch_size
    if args.lr_decay_iters is None:
        args.lr_decay_iters = args.train_iters
    lr_decay_steps = args.lr_decay_iters * args.global_batch_size
    wd_incr_steps = args.train_iters * args.global_batch_size
    wsd_decay_steps = None
    if args.lr_wsd_decay_iters is not None:
        wsd_decay_steps = args.lr_wsd_decay_iters * args.global_batch_size
    if args.lr_warmup_fraction is not None:
        lr_warmup_steps = args.lr_warmup_fraction * lr_decay_steps
    else:
        lr_warmup_steps = args.lr_warmup_iters * args.global_batch_size

    opt_param_scheduler = OptimizerParamScheduler(
        optimizer,
        init_lr=args.lr_warmup_init,
        max_lr=args.lr,
        min_lr=args.min_lr,
        lr_warmup_steps=lr_warmup_steps,
        lr_decay_steps=lr_decay_steps,
        lr_decay_style=args.lr_decay_style,
        start_wd=args.start_weight_decay,
        end_wd=args.end_weight_decay,
        wd_incr_steps=wd_incr_steps,
        wd_incr_style=args.weight_decay_incr_style,
        use_checkpoint_opt_param_scheduler=args.use_checkpoint_opt_param_scheduler,
        override_opt_param_scheduler=args.override_opt_param_scheduler,
        wsd_decay_steps=wsd_decay_steps,
        lr_wsd_decay_style=args.lr_wsd_decay_style,
    )

    return opt_param_scheduler


def _noop_init_state_fn(*args, **kwargs) -> None:
    return None


def _disable_distributed_optimizer_state_initialization(optimizer: MegatronOptimizer) -> None:
    for megatron_optimizer in getattr(optimizer, "chained_optimizers", [optimizer]):
        if megatron_optimizer.__class__.__name__ == "DistributedOptimizer":
            megatron_optimizer.init_state_fn = _noop_init_state_fn


@contextmanager
def _patch_megatron_adam(adam_cls):
    import megatron.core.optimizer as megatron_optimizer
    import megatron.core.optimizer.distrib_optimizer as megatron_distrib_optimizer

    missing = object()
    old_adam = megatron_optimizer.Adam
    old_cpu_adam = getattr(megatron_optimizer, "CPUAdam", missing)
    old_distrib_adam = megatron_distrib_optimizer.Adam
    try:
        megatron_optimizer.Adam = adam_cls
        if old_cpu_adam is not missing:
            megatron_optimizer.CPUAdam = adam_cls

182	    """Create and configure the optimizer learning-rate/weight-decay scheduler.
183	
184	    This configures iteration-based schedules derived from the global batch size
185	    and run-time arguments.
186	
187	    Args:
188	        args (Namespace): Training/runtime arguments (argparse namespace).
189	        optimizer (MegatronOptimizer): Megatron optimizer bound to the model.
190	
191	    Returns:
192	        OptimizerParamScheduler: Initialized scheduler bound to ``optimizer``.
193	    """
194	    # Iteration-based training. ``train_iters`` is an estimate of the total
195	    # number of training steps — it's only used to size Megatron's LR decay
196	    # schedule (and ``lr_decay_iters`` defaults to it). With variable per-rollout
197	    # sample counts (dynamic sampling / filtering / custom step splitter) the
198	    # *actual* total can drift; the schedule still tracks the true progress via
199	    # ``opt_param_scheduler.num_steps`` (samples consumed, also persisted across
200	    # resume), so the worst case is the cosine/linear schedule reaches its
201	    # plateau slightly early or late. Pass ``--lr-decay-iters`` explicitly if you
202	    # need exact decay control.
203	    args.train_iters = args.num_rollout * args.rollout_batch_size * args.n_samples_per_prompt // args.global_batch_size
204	    if args.lr_decay_iters is None:
205	        args.lr_decay_iters = args.train_iters
206	    lr_decay_steps = args.lr_decay_iters * args.global_batch_size
207	    wd_incr_steps = args.train_iters * args.global_batch_size
208	    wsd_decay_steps = None
209	    if args.lr_wsd_decay_iters is not None:
210	        wsd_decay_steps = args.lr_wsd_decay_iters * args.global_batch_size
211	    if args.lr_warmup_fraction is not None:
212	        lr_warmup_steps = args.lr_warmup_fraction * lr_decay_steps
213	    else:
214	        lr_warmup_steps = args.lr_warmup_iters * args.global_batch_size
215	
216	    opt_param_scheduler = OptimizerParamScheduler(
217	        optimizer,
218	        init_lr=args.lr_warmup_init,
219	        max_lr=args.lr,
220	        min_lr=args.min_lr,
221	        lr_warmup_steps=lr_warmup_steps,
222	        lr_decay_steps=lr_decay_steps,
223	        lr_decay_style=args.lr_decay_style,
224	        start_wd=args.start_weight_decay,
225	        end_wd=args.end_weight_decay,
226	        wd_incr_steps=wd_incr_steps,
227	        wd_incr_style=args.weight_decay_incr_style,
228	        use_checkpoint_opt_param_scheduler=args.use_checkpoint_opt_param_scheduler,
229	        override_opt_param_scheduler=args.override_opt_param_scheduler,
230	        wsd_decay_steps=wsd_decay_steps,
231	        lr_wsd_decay_style=args.lr_wsd_decay_style,
232	    )
233	
234	    return opt_param_scheduler

    """Persist a training checkpoint safely with forward hooks disabled.

    Args:
        iteration (int): Current global iteration number.
        model (Sequence[DDP]): Sequence of DDP-wrapped model chunks.
        optimizer (MegatronOptimizer): Optimizer instance.
        opt_param_scheduler (OptimizerParamScheduler): LR/WD scheduler.

    args = get_args()
    if should_disable_forward_pre_hook(args):

def initialize_model_and_optimizer(
    args: Namespace, role: str = "actor"
) -> tuple[list[DDP], MegatronOptimizer | None, OptimizerParamScheduler | None, int]:
    """Initialize model(s), optimizer, scheduler, and load from checkpoint.

    Args:
        args (Namespace): Runtime arguments.
        role (str): Logical role of the model (e.g., "actor", "critic").

    Returns:
        tuple[list[DDP], MegatronOptimizer | None, OptimizerParamScheduler | None, int]:
            DDP-wrapped model chunks, optimizer, scheduler, and iteration index.
    """

    if torch.version.hip:
        import megatron.core.dist_checkpointing.strategies.filesystem_async as filesystem_async_module

        from slime.utils.rocm_checkpoint_writer import ROCmFileSystemWriterAsync

        filesystem_async_module.FileSystemWriterAsync = ROCmFileSystemWriterAsync
        print("[ROCm] Applied FileSystemWriterAsync patch for HIP compatibility")

    model, optimizer, opt_param_scheduler = setup_model_and_optimizer(args, role)
    model[0].role = role
    reinit_critic_output_layer = _critic_output_layer_needs_reinit(args, model, role)
    clear_memory()
    iteration, _ = load_checkpoint(
        model,
        optimizer,
        opt_param_scheduler,
        checkpointing_context={},
    )
    if reinit_critic_output_layer:
        _reinitialize_critic_output_layer(args, model)
        if (args.fp16 or args.bf16) and optimizer is not None:
            optimizer.reload_model_params()
    clear_memory()

    return model, optimizer, opt_param_scheduler, iteration

# This is to align the timing of garbage collection across ranks.
        assert args.manual_gc_interval >= 0, "Manual garbage collection interval should be larger than or equal to 0"
        gc.disable()
        gc.collect()

    # Disable forward pre-hook to start training to ensure that errors in checkpoint loading
    # or random initialization don't propagate to all ranks in first all-gather (which is a
    # no-op if things work correctly).
    if should_disable_forward_pre_hook(args):
        disable_forward_pre_hook(model, param_sync=False)
        # Also remove param_sync_func temporarily so that sync calls made in
        # `forward_backward_func` are no-ops.
        param_sync_func = config.param_sync_func
        config.param_sync_func = None
        pre_hook_enabled = False

    num_steps_per_rollout = len(num_microbatches)
    microbatch_pbar = tqdm(
        total=sum(num_microbatches),
        desc=f"{getattr(model[0], 'role', 'actor')} train",
        unit="microbatch",
        dynamic_ncols=True,
        leave=False,
        disable=_disable_tqdm_for_non_main_rank(),
    )

    # Run training iterations till done.
    for step_id in range(num_steps_per_rollout):

        # Run training step.
        loss_dict, grad_norm = train_one_step(
            args,
            rollout_id,
            step_id,
            data_iterator,
            model,
            optimizer,
            opt_param_scheduler,
            num_microbatches[step_id],
            global_batch_sizes[step_id],
            microbatch_pbar=microbatch_pbar,
        )

        if step_id == 0:
            # Enable forward pre-hook after training step has successfully run. All subsequent
            # forward passes will use the forward pre-hook / `param_sync_func` in
            # `forward_backward_func`.
            if should_disable_forward_pre_hook(args):
                enable_forward_pre_hook(model)
                config.param_sync_func = param_sync_func
                pre_hook_enabled = True

        if args.enable_mtp_training:
            from megatron.core.transformer.multi_token_prediction import MTPLossLoggingHelper

            mtp_loss_scale = 1 / num_microbatches[step_id]
            tracker = MTPLossLoggingHelper.tracker
            if "values" in tracker:
                values = tracker["values"]
                if tracker.get("reduce_group") is not None:
                    torch.distributed.all_reduce(values, group=tracker.get("reduce_group"))
                if tracker.get("avg_group") is not None:
                    torch.distributed.all_reduce(values, group=tracker["avg_group"], op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.AVG)
                # Multi-head MTP: tracker["values"] is [num_mtp_layers]; aggregate below.
                mtp_losses = tracker["values"] * mtp_loss_scale
                MTPLossLoggingHelper.clean_loss_in_tracker()

                # CI check: verify MTP loss is within expected bounds
                if args.ci_test:
                    from slime.backends.megatron_utils.ci_utils import check_mtp_loss

                    check_mtp_loss(mtp_losses.sum().item())

        # per train step log.
        if (
            mpu.get_data_parallel_rank(with_context_parallel=True) == 0
            and mpu.get_tensor_model_parallel_rank() == 0
            and mpu.get_pipeline_model_parallel_rank() == mpu.get_pipeline_model_parallel_world_size() - 1
        ):
            accumulated_step_id = rollout_id * num_steps_per_rollout + step_id
            role = getattr(model[0], "role", "actor")
            role_tag = "" if role == "actor" else f"{role}-"
            log_dict = {
                f"train/{role_tag}{key}": val.mean().item() if isinstance(val, torch.Tensor) else val
                for key, val in loss_dict.items()
            }
            log_dict[f"train/{role_tag}grad_norm"] = grad_norm
            if args.enable_mtp_training:
                for _i in range(mtp_losses.shape[0]):
                    log_dict[f"train/{role_tag}mtp_{_i + 1}_loss"] = mtp_losses[_i].item()
                log_dict[f"train/{role_tag}mtp_loss"] = mtp_losses.sum().item()

            for param_group_id, param_group in enumerate(optimizer.param_groups):
                log_dict[f"train/{role_tag}lr-pg_{param_group_id}"] = opt_param_scheduler.get_lr(param_group)

            # Per-step gbs — uneven step sizes are easy to miss without this.
            log_dict[f"train/{role_tag}global_batch_size"] = global_batch_sizes[step_id]
            log_dict["train/step"] = accumulated_step_id
            logging_utils.log(args, log_dict, step_key="train/step")

            if args.ci_test and "train/train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff" in log_dict:
                threshold = args.ci_train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff_threshold
                assert log_dict["train/train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff"] <= threshold, f"{threshold=} {log_dict=}"

            if args.ci_test and not args.ci_disable_kl_checker:
                if step_id == 0 and "train/ppo_kl" in log_dict and "train/pg_clipfrac" in log_dict:
                    # TODO: figure out why KL is not exactly zero when using PPO loss with KL clipping, and whether this is expected behavior or a bug.
                    assert log_dict["train/ppo_kl"] < 1e-8, f"{log_dict=}"
                # R3 replays rollout routing for the actor path, while ref
                # log-probs are computed with normal routing. The initial
                # actor/ref KL is therefore not expected to be exactly zero.
                if (
                    accumulated_step_id == 0
                    and not getattr(args, "use_rollout_routing_replay", False)
                    and "train/kl_loss" in log_dict
                ):
                    assert log_dict["train/kl_loss"] < 1e-8, f"{log_dict=}"

            logger.info(f"{role_tag}step {accumulated_step_id}: {log_dict}")

            if args.ci_save_grad_norm is not None:
                ci_save_grad_norm_path = args.ci_save_grad_norm.format(
                    role=role,
                    rollout_id=rollout_id,
                    step_id=step_id,
                )
                torch.save(grad_norm, ci_save_grad_norm_path)
            elif args.ci_load_grad_norm is not None:
                ci_load_grad_norm_path = args.ci_load_grad_norm.format(
                    role=role,
                    rollout_id=rollout_id,
                    step_id=step_id,
                )
                expected_grad_norm = torch.load(ci_load_grad_norm_path)
                assert math.isclose(
                    grad_norm,
                    expected_grad_norm,
                    rel_tol=0.01,
                    abs_tol=0.01,
                ), f"grad norm mismatch: {grad_norm} != {expected_grad_norm}"
    microbatch_pbar.close()
    # Close out pre-hooks if using distributed optimizer and overlapped param gather.
    if pre_hook_enabled:
        disable_forward_pre_hook(model)

def setup_model_and_optimizer(
    args: Namespace,
    role: str = "actor",
) -> tuple[list[DDP], MegatronOptimizer | None, OptimizerParamScheduler | None]:
    """Build model(s), wrap with DDP, and construct optimizer and scheduler.

    Args:
        args (Namespace): Training/runtime arguments (argparse namespace).
        role (str): Logical role of the model (e.g., "actor", "critic").
        no_wd_decay_cond (Callable[..., bool] | None): Predicate to exclude
            parameters from weight decay.
        scale_lr_cond (Callable[..., bool] | None): Predicate to scale LR for
            selected parameter groups.
        lr_mult (float): Global learning-rate multiplier for the optimizer.

    Returns:
        tuple[list[DDP], MegatronOptimizer | None, OptimizerParamScheduler | None]:
            - List of model chunks wrapped by ``DDP``.
            - The constructed ``MegatronOptimizer`` instance.
            - The learning-rate/weight-decay scheduler tied to the optimizer.
    """
    assert not args.moe_use_upcycling
    assert args.load is not None or args.pretrained_checkpoint is not None

    model = get_model(get_model_provider_func(args, role), ModelType.encoder_or_decoder)

    if args.num_rollout == 0:
        args.no_load_optim = True
        return model, None, None

    # Optimizer
    kwargs = {}
    for f in dataclasses.fields(OptimizerConfig):
        if hasattr(args, f.name):
            kwargs[f.name] = getattr(args, f.name)
    config = OptimizerConfig(**kwargs)
    config.timers = None

    if args.use_stateless_adam:
        assert config.optimizer == "adam", "Stateless Adam only supports --optimizer adam."
        assert args.no_save_optim, "Stateless Adam does not save Adam moment states. Please set --no-save-optim."

    optimizer_context = _patch_megatron_adam(StatelessAdam) if args.use_stateless_adam else nullcontext()
    with optimizer_context:
        optimizer = get_megatron_optimizer(
            config=config,
            model_chunks=model,
            use_gloo_process_groups=args.enable_gloo_process_groups,
        )
    if args.use_stateless_adam:
        _disable_distributed_optimizer_state_initialization(optimizer)
    opt_param_scheduler = get_optimizer_param_scheduler(args, optimizer)
    return model, optimizer, opt_param_scheduler


def enable_forward_pre_hook(model_chunks: Sequence[DDP]) -> None:
    """Enable forward pre-hooks for provided DDP-wrapped model chunks.

    Args:
        model_chunks (Sequence[DDP]): Sequence of DDP modules to enable hooks on.
    """
    for model_chunk in model_chunks:
        assert isinstance(model_chunk, DDP)
        model_chunk.enable_forward_pre_hook()


def disable_forward_pre_hook(model_chunks: Sequence[DDP], param_sync: bool = True) -> None:
    """Disable forward pre-hooks for provided DDP-wrapped model chunks.

    Args:
        model_chunks (Sequence[DDP]): Sequence of DDP modules to disable hooks on.
        param_sync (bool): Whether to synchronize parameters when disabling.
    """
    for model_chunk in model_chunks:
        assert isinstance(model_chunk, DDP)
        model_chunk.disable_forward_pre_hook(param_sync=param_sync)

import logging
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path

# TODO: may need to copy those 2 functions and do refactoring.
from megatron.training.checkpointing import load_checkpoint as _load_checkpoint_megatron
from megatron.training.checkpointing import save_checkpoint
from megatron.training.global_vars import get_args

try:
    # Here we patch out the `validate_non_overlapping_shards_metadata` in both functions
    # because it is really slow for large models with many shards.
    # TODO: find a less hacky way to do this.
    import torch.distributed as dist
    import torch.distributed._shard.sharding_spec as shard_spec
    from torch.distributed._shard.sharded_tensor import ShardedTensor
    from torch.distributed._shard.sharded_tensor.metadata import ShardedTensorMetadata
    from torch.distributed._shard.sharded_tensor.shard import Shard
    from torch.distributed._shard.sharded_tensor.utils import _parse_and_validate_remote_device
    from torch.distributed._shard.sharding_spec.api import EnumerableShardingSpec

    def __post_init__(self):
        pass

    EnumerableShardingSpec.__post_init__ = __post_init__

    @classmethod
    def _init_from_local_shards_and_global_metadata(  # type: ignore[override]
        cls,
        local_shards: list[Shard],
        sharded_tensor_metadata: ShardedTensorMetadata,
        process_group=None,
        init_rrefs=False,
        sharding_spec=None,
    ) -> ShardedTensor:
        """
        Initialize a ShardedTensor with local shards and a global
        ShardedTensorMetadata built on each rank.

        Warning: This API is experimental and subject to change. It does
                 not do cross rank validations, and fully rely on the user
                 for the correctness of sharded_tensor_metadata on each rank
        """
        process_group = cls._normalize_pg(process_group)
        current_rank = dist.get_rank()  # intentional to get global rank

        shards_metadata = sharded_tensor_metadata.shards_metadata

        local_shard_metadatas = []

        # collect local shard metadatas from the global sharded_tensor_metadata
        for shard_metadata in shards_metadata:  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
            rank, local_device = _parse_and_validate_remote_device(process_group, shard_metadata.placement)

            if current_rank == rank:
                local_shard_metadatas.append(shard_metadata)

from pathlib import Path

from transformers import AutoConfig

from .common import load_model_hf_weights
from .deepseek import deepseek_hf_tensor
from .glm import glm4_hf_tensor, glm4_moe_hf_tensor
from .qwen import mimo_hf_tensor, minimax_m2_hf_tensor, qwen_hf_tensor, qwen_moe_hf_tensor
from .qwen3_5 import qwen3_5_hf_tensor
from .qwen3_next import qwen3_next_hf_tensor

_LOADERS = {
    "deepseek_v3": deepseek_hf_tensor,
    "deepseek_v32": deepseek_hf_tensor,
    "glm4": glm4_hf_tensor,
    "glm4_moe": glm4_moe_hf_tensor,
    "glm4_moe_lite": deepseek_hf_tensor,
    "glm_moe_dsa": deepseek_hf_tensor,
    "kimi_k2": deepseek_hf_tensor,
    "llama": qwen_hf_tensor,
    "mimo": mimo_hf_tensor,
    "minimax_m2": minimax_m2_hf_tensor,
    "qwen2": qwen_hf_tensor,
    "qwen2_moe": qwen_moe_hf_tensor,
    "qwen3": qwen_hf_tensor,
    "qwen3_5": qwen3_5_hf_tensor,
    "qwen3_5_moe": qwen3_5_hf_tensor,
    "qwen3_moe": qwen_moe_hf_tensor,
    "qwen3_next": qwen3_next_hf_tensor,
}


def supports_hf_weight_loading(path: str | Path) -> bool:
    config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(path, trust_remote_code=True)
    return config.model_type in _LOADERS


def load_hf_weights(args, model, path: str | Path) -> None:
    config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(path, trust_remote_code=True)
    try:
        get_hf_tensor = _LOADERS[config.model_type]
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported HuggingFace model type: {config.model_type}") from exc
    load_model_hf_weights(args, model, path, config, get_hf_tensor)

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Extract the critic's warmup value loss from a slime training log.
3	
4	slime reports per-optimizer-step training metrics only on stdout, via
5	`slime/backends/megatron_utils/model.py`:
6	
7	    logger.info(f"{role_tag}step {accumulated_step_id}: {log_dict}")
8	
9	so for the critic the lines look like
10	
11	    critic-step 0: {'train/critic-value_loss': 5.91, 'train/critic-value_clipfrac': 0.0, ...}
12	
13	Rollout-level metrics are emitted the same way but keyed by rollout id rather
14	than optimizer step, with a label instead of `step N`:
15	
16	    rollout 0: {'rollout/rewards': 0.125, 'rollout/round_number': 4.0, ...}
17	    perf 0:    {'rollout/response_len/mean': 244.4, ...}
18	
19	Which of those appear depends on the stage, which is why both are parsed.
20	`rollout N:` comes from the training actor and is only logged on rollouts where
21	the actor trains (slime calls it inside `train_actor`), so a critic-only warmup
22	stage has none. `perf N:` is logged by the RolloutManager on every rollout, so
23	it is the stage-independent evidence that episodes were really generated.
24	
25	There is no jsonl or csv sink for any of these, hence this parser.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract the critic's warmup value loss from a slime training log.

slime reports per-optimizer-step training metrics only on stdout, via
`slime/backends/megatron_utils/model.py`:

    logger.info(f"{role_tag}step {accumulated_step_id}: {log_dict}")

so for the critic the lines look like

    critic-step 0: {'train/critic-value_loss': 5.91, 'train/critic-value_clipfrac': 0.0, ...}

Rollout-level metrics are emitted the same way but keyed by rollout id rather
than optimizer step, with a label instead of `step N`:

    rollout 0: {'rollout/rewards': 0.125, 'rollout/round_number': 4.0, ...}
    perf 0:    {'rollout/response_len/mean': 244.4, ...}

Which of those appear depends on the stage, which is why both are parsed.
`rollout N:` comes from the training actor and is only logged on rollouts where
the actor trains (slime calls it inside `train_actor`), so a critic-only warmup
stage has none. `perf N:` is logged by the RolloutManager on every rollout, so
it is the stage-independent evidence that episodes were really generated.

There is no jsonl or csv sink for any of these, hence this parser.

Usage:
    python3 tools/parse_value_loss.py train.log --warmup-steps 2 --out summary.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ast
import json
import re
import sys

STEP_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s\]])(?P<role>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*-)?step\s+(?P<step>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")

# `<label> <id>: {...}` for any label that is not a `step` line, i.e. the
# rollout-level metrics. Anchored on " - " so it matches the logger's
# "<file>.py:<line> - " prefix and not arbitrary prose.
ROLLOUT_RE = re.compile(r" - (?P<label>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s+(?P<id>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")


def _coerce(value):
    try:
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _payload(text: str) -> dict | None:
    try:
        payload = ast.literal_eval(text)
    except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
        return None
    return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else None


def parse(paths: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """Return one record per metric line, tagged `step` or `rollout`."""
    records: list[dict] = []
    for path in paths:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
            for line in fh:
                line = line.rstrip("\n")
                m = STEP_RE.search(line)
                if m:
                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
                    if payload is None:
                        continue
                    role = (m.group("role") or "").rstrip("-") or "actor"
                    records.append(
                        {"kind": "step", "role": role, "step": int(m.group("step")), "metrics": payload}
                    )
                    continue
                m = ROLLOUT_RE.search(line)
                if m:
                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
                    if payload is None:
                        continue
                    records.append(
                        {
                            "kind": "rollout",
                            "label": m.group("label"),
                            "step": int(m.group("id")),
                            "metrics": payload,
                        }
                    )
    return records


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("logs", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--warmup-steps",
        type=int,
        default=0,
        help="number of leading critic optimizer steps to average over (0 = all critic steps)",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    records = parse(args.logs)

    critic_steps = []
    for rec in records:
        if rec["kind"] != "step":
            continue
        hit = next((k for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_loss")), None)
        if hit is None:
            continue
        value = _coerce(rec["metrics"][hit])
        if value is None:
            continue
        critic_steps.append(
            {
                "step": rec["step"],
                "value_loss": value,
                "value_clipfrac": _coerce(
                    next((rec["metrics"][k] for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_clipfrac")), None)
                ),
            }
        )
    critic_steps.sort(key=lambda r: r["step"])

    rewards = []
    for rec in records:
        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items():
            if "reward" in key and not key.endswith(("_std", "_max", "_min")):
                coerced = _coerce(value)
                if coerced is not None:
                    rewards.append({"step": rec["step"], "key": key, "value": coerced})

    # Evidence that episodes were really generated in this stage, independent of
    # whether the actor trained: the RolloutManager reports response-length
    # statistics once per rollout. A stage that generated nothing has neither.
    #
    # Only `rollout/response_len/mean` (the RolloutManager's `perf N:` line) is
    # averaged. slime also emits `rollout/response_lengths` from the actor side,
    # but it is a *different* quantity -- it counts the tokens the trainer sees,
    # including the observation turns fed back into the context, so it runs ~70%
    # higher. Averaging the two together produced a blended figure that meant
    # nothing and was not comparable between stages, since the actor-side metric
    # only exists on rollouts where the actor trains.
    rollout_ids = {rec["step"] for rec in records if rec["kind"] == "rollout"}
    response_lens = [
        _coerce(value)
        for rec in records
        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items()
        if key.endswith("response_len/mean")
    ]
    response_lens = [v for v in response_lens if v is not None]

    window = critic_steps[: args.warmup_steps] if args.warmup_steps > 0 else critic_steps
    losses = [r["value_loss"] for r in window]

    summary = {
        "n_critic_steps": len(critic_steps),
        "rollouts_generated": len(rollout_ids),
        "mean_response_len": (sum(response_lens) / len(response_lens)) if response_lens else None,
        "warmup_window": len(window),
        "critic_steps": critic_steps,
        "first_value_loss": critic_steps[0]["value_loss"] if critic_steps else None,
        "warmup_value_loss_mean": (sum(losses) / len(losses)) if losses else None,
        "warmup_value_loss_max": max(losses) if losses else None,
        "warmup_value_loss_min": min(losses) if losses else None,
        "rewards": rewards[:50],
        "mean_reward": (sum(r["value"] for r in rewards) / len(rewards)) if rewards else None,
    }

    if args.out:
        with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(summary, fh, indent=2)

    print(f"critic optimizer steps found: {summary['n_critic_steps']}")
    if not critic_steps:
        print("NO value_loss METRICS FOUND -- the critic never took an optimizer step.", file=sys.stderr)
        print("Check that --advantage-estimator ppo is set and that training reached the critic.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    print(f"{'step':>6}  {'value_loss':>14}  {'value_clipfrac':>14}")
    for rec in critic_steps:
        clip = "n/a" if rec["value_clipfrac"] is None else f"{rec['value_clipfrac']:.4f}"
        print(f"{rec['step']:>6}  {rec['value_loss']:>14.6f}  {clip:>14}")
    print(f"\nwarmup window = first {summary['warmup_window']} critic step(s)")
    print(f"warmup value_loss mean = {summary['warmup_value_loss_mean']:.6f}")
    print(f"rollouts generated = {summary['rollouts_generated']}", end="")
    if summary["mean_response_len"] is not None:
        print(f" (mean response {summary['mean_response_len']:.1f} tokens)", end="")
    print()
    if summary["mean_reward"] is not None:
        print(f"mean reward (episode pass rate) ~= {summary['mean_reward']:.4f}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

13	Rollout-level metrics are emitted the same way but keyed by rollout id rather
14	than optimizer step, with a label instead of `step N`:
15	
16	    rollout 0: {'rollout/rewards': 0.125, 'rollout/round_number': 4.0, ...}
17	    perf 0:    {'rollout/response_len/mean': 244.4, ...}
18	
19	Which of those appear depends on the stage, which is why both are parsed.
20	`rollout N:` comes from the training actor and is only logged on rollouts where
21	the actor trains (slime calls it inside `train_actor`), so a critic-only warmup
22	stage has none. `perf N:` is logged by the RolloutManager on every rollout, so
23	it is the stage-independent evidence that episodes were really generated.
24	
25	There is no jsonl or csv sink for any of these, hence this parser.
26	
27	Usage:
28	    python3 tools/parse_value_loss.py train.log --warmup-steps 2 --out summary.json
29	"""
30	
31	from __future__ import annotations
32	
33	import argparse
34	import ast
35	import json
36	import re
37	import sys
38	
39	STEP_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s\]])(?P<role>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*-)?step\s+(?P<step>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")
40	
41	# `<label> <id>: {...}` for any label that is not a `step` line, i.e. the
42	# rollout-level metrics. Anchored on " - " so it matches the logger's
43	# "<file>.py:<line> - " prefix and not arbitrary prose.
44	ROLLOUT_RE = re.compile(r" - (?P<label>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s+(?P<id>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")
45	
46	
47	def _coerce(value):
48	    try:
49	        return float(value)
50	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
51	        return None
52	
53	
54	def _payload(text: str) -> dict | None:
55	    try:
56	        payload = ast.literal_eval(text)
57	    except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
58	        return None
59	    return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
60	
61	
62	def parse(paths: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
63	    """Return one record per metric line, tagged `step` or `rollout`."""
64	    records: list[dict] = []
65	    for path in paths:
66	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
67	            for line in fh:
68	                line = line.rstrip("\n")
69	                m = STEP_RE.search(line)
70	                if m:
71	                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
72	                    if payload is None:
73	                        continue
74	                    role = (m.group("role") or "").rstrip("-") or "actor"
75	                    records.append(
76	                        {"kind": "step", "role": role, "step": int(m.group("step")), "metrics": payload}
77	                    )
78	                    continue
79	                m = ROLLOUT_RE.search(line)
80	                if m:
81	                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
82	                    if payload is None:
83	                        continue
84	                    records.append(
85	                        {
86	                            "kind": "rollout",
87	                            "label": m.group("label"),
88	                            "step": int(m.group("id")),
89	                            "metrics": payload,
90	                        }
91	                    )
92	    return records
93	
94	
95	def main() -> int:
96	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
97	    ap.add_argument("logs", nargs="+")
98	    ap.add_argument(
99	        "--warmup-steps",
100	        type=int,
101	        default=0,
102	        help="number of leading critic optimizer steps to average over (0 = all critic steps)",
103	    )
104	    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
105	    args = ap.parse_args()
106	
107	    records = parse(args.logs)
108	
109	    critic_steps = []
110	    for rec in records:
111	        if rec["kind"] != "step":
112	            continue
113	        hit = next((k for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_loss")), None)
114	        if hit is None:
115	            continue
116	        value = _coerce(rec["metrics"][hit])
117	        if value is None:
118	            continue
119	        critic_steps.append(
120	            {
121	                "step": rec["step"],
122	                "value_loss": value,
123	                "value_clipfrac": _coerce(
124	                    next((rec["metrics"][k] for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_clipfrac")), None)
125	                ),
126	            }
127	        )
128	    critic_steps.sort(key=lambda r: r["step"])
129	
130	    rewards = []
131	    for rec in records:
132	        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items():
133	            if "reward" in key and not key.endswith(("_std", "_max", "_min")):
134	                coerced = _coerce(value)
135	                if coerced is not None:
136	                    rewards.append({"step": rec["step"], "key": key, "value": coerced})
137	
138	    # Evidence that episodes were really generated in this stage, independent of
139	    # whether the actor trained: the RolloutManager reports response-length
140	    # statistics once per rollout. A stage that generated nothing has neither.
141	    #
142	    # Only `rollout/response_len/mean` (the RolloutManager's `perf N:` line) is
143	    # averaged. slime also emits `rollout/response_lengths` from the actor side,
144	    # but it is a *different* quantity -- it counts the tokens the trainer sees,
145	    # including the observation turns fed back into the context, so it runs ~70%
146	    # higher. Averaging the two together produced a blended figure that meant
147	    # nothing and was not comparable between stages, since the actor-side metric
148	    # only exists on rollouts where the actor trains.
149	    rollout_ids = {rec["step"] for rec in records if rec["kind"] == "rollout"}
150	    response_lens = [
151	        _coerce(value)
152	        for rec in records
153	        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items()
154	        if key.endswith("response_len/mean")
155	    ]
156	    response_lens = [v for v in response_lens if v is not None]
157	
158	    window = critic_steps[: args.warmup_steps] if args.warmup_steps > 0 else critic_steps
159	    losses = [r["value_loss"] for r in window]
160	
161	    summary = {
162	        "n_critic_steps": len(critic_steps),
163	        "rollouts_generated": len(rollout_ids),
164	        "mean_response_len": (sum(response_lens) / len(response_lens)) if response_lens else None,
165	        "warmup_window": len(window),
166	        "critic_steps": critic_steps,
167	        "first_value_loss": critic_steps[0]["value_loss"] if critic_steps else None,
168	        "warmup_value_loss_mean": (sum(losses) / len(losses)) if losses else None,
169	        "warmup_value_loss_max": max(losses) if losses else None,
170	        "warmup_value_loss_min": min(losses) if losses else None,
171	        "rewards": rewards[:50],
172	        "mean_reward": (sum(r["value"] for r in rewards) / len(rewards)) if rewards else None,
173	    }
174	
175	    if args.out:
176	        with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
177	            json.dump(summary, fh, indent=2)
178	
179	    print(f"critic optimizer steps found: {summary['n_critic_steps']}")
180	    if not critic_steps:
181	        print("NO value_loss METRICS FOUND -- the critic never took an optimizer step.", file=sys.stderr)
182	        print("Check that --advantage-estimator ppo is set and that training reached the critic.", file=sys.stderr)
183	        return 2
184	    print(f"{'step':>6}  {'value_loss':>14}  {'value_clipfrac':>14}")
185	    for rec in critic_steps:
186	        clip = "n/a" if rec["value_clipfrac"] is None else f"{rec['value_clipfrac']:.4f}"
187	        print(f"{rec['step']:>6}  {rec['value_loss']:>14.6f}  {clip:>14}")
188	    print(f"\nwarmup window = first {summary['warmup_window']} critic step(s)")
189	    print(f"warmup value_loss mean = {summary['warmup_value_loss_mean']:.6f}")
190	    print(f"rollouts generated = {summary['rollouts_generated']}", end="")
191	    if summary["mean_response_len"] is not None:
192	        print(f" (mean response {summary['mean_response_len']:.1f} tokens)", end="")
193	    print()
194	    if summary["mean_reward"] is not None:
195	        print(f"mean reward (episode pass rate) ~= {summary['mean_reward']:.4f}")
196	    return 0
197	
198	
199	if __name__ == "__main__":
200	    raise SystemExit(main())
201

def parse_args(add_custom_arguments=None):
    # Users may call `parse_args` very early, thus we ensure logger is configured here
    configure_logger()

    add_slime_arguments = get_slime_extra_args_provider(add_custom_arguments)

    pre = _pre_parse_mode()
    skip_sglang = pre.debug_train_only or pre.load_debug_rollout_data is not None

    # Phase 1: Parse sglang args independently (separate parser, parse_known_args).
    # Skipped when sglang servers are not needed.
    sglang_ns = None
    if not skip_sglang:
        sglang_ns = sglang_parse_args()

    # Phase 2: Parse megatron + slime args.
    # Uses ignore_unknown_args=True so that --sglang-* and pre-parsed CLI flags
    # are silently ignored by the megatron parser.
    from slime.backends.megatron_utils.arguments import megatron_parse_args
    from slime.backends.megatron_utils.arguments import validate_args as megatron_validate_args

    args = megatron_parse_args(
        extra_args_provider=add_slime_arguments,
        skip_hf_validate=pre.debug_rollout_only,
    )

    # Merge pre-parsed args into the main namespace
    for key, value in vars(pre).items():
        setattr(args, key, value)

    # Merge sglang args into the main namespace
    if sglang_ns is not None:
        for key, value in vars(sglang_ns).items():
            setattr(args, key, value)

    slime_validate_args(args)

    if not args.debug_rollout_only:
        megatron_validate_args(args)

    if not args.debug_train_only:
        sglang_validate_args(args)

    return args


def _apply_megatron_role_overrides(base_args, overrides, role):
    role_args = copy.deepcopy(base_args)

return RayTrainGroup(
        args=args,
        num_nodes=num_nodes,
        num_gpus_per_node=num_gpus_per_node,
        pg=pg,
        num_gpus_per_actor=0.4,
        role=role,
        with_ref=with_ref,
        with_opd_teacher=with_opd_teacher,
        actor_cls=actor_cls,
    )


def create_actor_model(args, pgs, rollout_manager, actor_cls=None):
    actor_args = args
    if args.megatron_config_path is not None:
        from slime.utils.arguments import parse_megatron_role_args

        actor_args = parse_megatron_role_args(args, args.megatron_config_path, role="actor")

    actor_model_kwargs = {}
    if actor_cls is not None:
        actor_model_kwargs["actor_cls"] = actor_cls
    actor_model = allocate_train_group(
        args=actor_args,
        num_nodes=args.actor_num_nodes,
        num_gpus_per_node=args.actor_num_gpus_per_node,
        pg=pgs["actor"],
        with_ref=actor_args.kl_coef != 0 or actor_args.use_kl_loss,
        with_opd_teacher=actor_args.use_opd and actor_args.opd_type == "megatron",
        **actor_model_kwargs,
    )
    actor_start_rollout_ids = actor_model.create(rollout_manager=rollout_manager)
    return actor_model, actor_start_rollout_ids


def create_training_models(args, pgs, rollout_manager, actor_cls=None):
    actor_model, actor_start_rollout_ids = create_actor_model(args, pgs, rollout_manager, actor_cls=actor_cls)

    critic_model = None
    if args.use_critic and args.num_rollout != 0:
        from slime.utils.arguments import parse_megatron_role_args

        critic_args = (
            parse_megatron_role_args(args, args.megatron_config_path, role="critic")
            if args.megatron_config_path is not None
            else copy.deepcopy(args)
        )
        if args.megatron_config_path is None:
            critic_args.disable_param_buffers_cpu_backup = False

        critic_model = allocate_train_group(
            args=critic_args,
            num_nodes=args.critic_num_nodes,
            num_gpus_per_node=args.critic_num_gpus_per_node,
            pg=pgs["critic"],
            role="critic",
        )
        critic_start_rollout_ids = critic_model.create(rollout_manager=rollout_manager)

    # TODO how to decide rollout start id when critic is involved? For now we just require user to specify it via args.
    if critic_model is not None:
        start_rollout_ids = critic_start_rollout_ids
    else:
        start_rollout_ids = actor_start_rollout_ids

    assert len(set(start_rollout_ids)) == 1

    if args.start_rollout_id is None:
        args.start_rollout_id = start_rollout_ids[0]

    if args.rollout_global_dataset:
        ray.get(rollout_manager.load.remote(args.start_rollout_id - 1))

    return actor_model, critic_model


def create_rollout_manager(args, pg):
    from .rollout import RolloutManager

    rollout_manager_options = {
        "num_cpus": 1,
        "num_gpus": 0,
        "runtime_env": {"env_vars": add_default_ray_env_vars()},
    }
    if getattr(args, "rollout_data_transport", "object-store") == "nixl":
        rollout_manager_options["enable_tensor_transport"] = True
    rollout_manager = RolloutManager.options(**rollout_manager_options).remote(args, pg)

    # calculate num_rollout from num_epoch
    num_rollout_per_epoch = None
    if args.num_rollout is None:
        num_rollout_per_epoch = ray.get(rollout_manager.get_num_rollout_per_epoch.remote())
        args.num_rollout = num_rollout_per_epoch * args.num_epoch
        assert args.num_rollout > 0

    if args.check_weight_update_equal:
        ray.get(rollout_manager.check_weights.remote(action="snapshot"))
        ray.get(rollout_manager.check_weights.remote(action="reset_tensors"))

    if args.offload_rollout:
        ray.get(rollout_manager.offload.remote())

    return rollout_manager, num_rollout_per_epoch

def _set_default_megatron_args(args):
    # always use zero optimizer
    args.use_distributed_optimizer = True
    if not hasattr(args, "enable_gloo_process_groups"):
        args.enable_gloo_process_groups = True
    # TODO: maybe change this after megatron has good fp8 support
    args.bf16 = not args.fp16
    # Checkpoint I/O defaults: these keep checkpoint contents unchanged while
    # reducing repeated validation/planning work and parallelizing load.
    args.use_persistent_ckpt_worker = True
    args.ckpt_assume_constant_structure = True
    args.ckpt_fully_parallel_load = True
    # placeholders
    if args.seq_length is None:
        args.seq_length = 4096
    # Megatron also uses this value as YaRN's original context length. Preserve
    # the checkpoint/model value when the launcher supplied one explicitly.
    if args.max_position_embeddings is None:
        args.max_position_embeddings = args.seq_length
    # TODO: revisit this when megatron(dev) have solved the optimizer-cpu-offload ckpt saving bug
    args.dist_ckpt_save_pre_mcore_014 = True
    # compatible for megatron
    if hasattr(args, "rope_type") and args.rope_type is None:
        args.rope_type = "yarn" if args.multi_latent_attention else "rope"

    if args.vocab_size and not args.padded_vocab_size:
        args.padded_vocab_size = _vocab_size_with_padding(args.vocab_size, args)

    if not args.tokenizer_model and not args.tokenizer_type:
        logger.info("--tokenizer-model not set, use --hf-checkpoint as tokenizer model.")
        args.tokenizer_model = args.hf_checkpoint
        args.tokenizer_type = "HuggingFaceTokenizer"
    elif not args.tokenizer_model:
        logger.info("--tokenizer-model not set, use --hf-checkpoint as tokenizer model.")
        args.tokenizer_model = args.hf_checkpoint
    return args


# Public alias for external tools (e.g. convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py)
set_default_megatron_args = _set_default_megatron_args


def megatron_parse_args(extra_args_provider, skip_hf_validate=False):
    """Parse megatron args, validate HF config, and set defaults."""
    args = _megatron_parse_args(extra_args_provider=extra_args_provider, ignore_unknown_args=True)

    hf_config = None
    if args.hf_checkpoint and not skip_hf_validate:
        hf_config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(args.hf_checkpoint, trust_remote_code=True)
        _hf_validate_args(args, hf_config)

    if not skip_hf_validate:
        _validate_allgather_cp_supported(args, hf_config)

    args.rank = 0
    args.world_size = args.actor_num_nodes * args.actor_num_gpus_per_node
    args = _set_default_megatron_args(args)
    return args
